title: The Log Swing
lines: Jane and Pete want a swing at home.
Dad hangs a long rope on a big pine.
Pete gets a fine log to sit on.
He sets it on the rope. It slips off.
Pete holds the log on. It still slips off.
"Cut a hole in it," said Jane.
Jane and Dad cut a hole in the log.
The rope goes in the hole and holds it.
Pete gets on and Jane pulls him back.
"The best swing!" said Pete with a big smile.

questions.ask: What did Pete get to sit on?
questions.listenFor: A fine log. Line three says it. If your child is stuck, let them reread that line.

questions.ask: Why did Jane and Dad cut a hole in the log?
questions.listenFor: Because the log kept slipping off the rope, and the rope could go through the hole. Lines four to eight carry it.

questions.ask: What would you make a swing seat out of? Tell me why that.
questions.listenFor: Any answer counts. You are listening for a reason that shows they understood why the log kept slipping.
